title: Asking About a Roommate Swap

prompt.scenario: You are a second-year resident in Maple Hall. Your assigned roommate works an overnight hospital nursing shift and returns to the room at 4:30 AM, while you have 8:00 AM chemistry lectures every morning. Despite using sleep masks and earplugs, your conflicting sleep schedules leave both of you exhausted. Write an email to the residential life coordinator, Ms. Vega.
requirements: Explain the severe sleep disruption caused by opposing overnight work and early morning class schedules.
Describe the practical compromises both roommates have already attempted (sleep masks, quiet hours, desk lamps).
Inquire about room transfer policies or mutual swap options with other night-shift students.

modelEssay:
Dear Ms. Vega,

I am writing to respectfully request advice regarding a room transfer due to an unavoidable schedule incompatibility in Maple Hall, Room 218.

My roommate and I get along very well personally, but our daily schedules are completely inverted. He works an overnight patient-care shift at the hospital and returns at 4:30 AM to cook and get ready for bed, while I have mandatory 8:00 AM chemistry lectures every weekday. Over the past month, we have tried establishing strict quiet rules, utilizing low-wattage desk lamps, and wearing earplugs and sleep masks, but the door latches and necessary movement continue to wake us up. As a result, both of us are experiencing chronic exhaustion that affects our academic performance. Could you explain the procedure for a mutual room swap? Perhaps there is another resident working nocturnal shifts who would be an ideal match. Thank you for your guidance.

Sincerely,
Alex Morgan

title: Correcting a Course Registration Error

prompt.scenario: You registered for your upcoming spring semester classes. When checking your student billing account, you discovered that Biology 210 (Cell Biology) was duplicated, appearing twice on your schedule and billing you for twenty-two credits instead of sixteen. Write an email to the academic registrar specialist, Ms. Alvarez.
requirements: Explain the duplicate enrollment error for Biology 210 displayed on your schedule portal.

Dear Ms. Alvarez,

I am writing to report a technical registration error on my student portal account and to request an administrative correction.

While reviewing my confirmed spring semester schedule this morning, I noticed that Biology 210 (Cell Biology, Section 02) is duplicated on my course roster. Although I registered for the lecture only once, the system created two identical four-credit entries with matching laboratory sections. Consequently, my registered total currently stands at twenty-two credit hours instead of sixteen, triggering an automated overload tuition surcharge on my bursar bill. Because tuition payments must be settled by this Friday, I want to resolve this billing inflation before financial aid funds are disbursed. Could your office please purge the duplicate Biology 210 enrollment and issue an updated billing statement? I have attached a screenshot of my registration confirmation. Thank you for your assistance.

Sincerely,
Alex Morgan
